title: I Followed the Community-Station Guest Pass Into the On-Air Booth They Closed

parts.text: I wore a guest pass for a 7:00 p.m. interview and the booth door said GUEST WITH PASS. Producer Nell closed it and ran the interview without me. The handbook said: PASS OPENS THE BOOTH. PRODUCER YIELDS TO THE BOOKED GUEST. I was forty-six, booked guest, holding a still of the closed door. Nell talked. "Producers are the mic." I photographed the pass, the handbook line, and the ON light without me. Then I logged a close. At 7:09 the program director asked why Nell's booth was closed on a valid pass. Petty is a word people use when their name is on the ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The program director can see a closed booth ON during a booked guest pass.

social.video_title: She closed the on-air booth on a valid guest pass — Part 1/2
social.description: Community station, a guest pass, and a closed booth. I logged the close. Would you have photographed the ON light?

parts.text: Nell called it a delay until the director asked for the log. I printed the close, the photo, and the handbook. The door opened. Nell delayed in the hallway and told producers delays were always about optics. Optics is a word producers use when a pass exists. Guest policy now has a second line: PRODUCERS YIELD. I keep the booth. Nell hallways. The interview finally sounds like a booking, not a hijack. Nobody thanked me, which is how you know a policy finally works. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.

social.description: Close log, opened door, and a second line. Was a delay ever a closed ON?
